analysis.investment_thesis: Cemindia (formerly ITD Cementation) is a specialized infrastructure contractor with genuinely strong ROCE of 27.6% and revenue that has nearly tripled from INR 3,809 Cr to INR 9,097 Cr in three years riding India's infrastructure supercycle. However, at INR 11,136 Cr market cap and P/E of 23.7x it has long since been discovered and priced for much of the good news.
key_strengths: Exceptional ROCE of 27.6% and ROE of 21.8% — rare for a construction company, signals strong project execution discipline
Revenue CAGR from FY22–FY25 ~34% with net profit growing from INR 69 Cr to INR 373 Cr — genuine earnings inflection
Promoter holding 67.46% with strong promoter backing (Renew Exim DMCC); skin in the game is solid
key_risks: FCF collapsed to INR 30 Cr in FY25 despite INR 373 Cr net profit — working capital intensity of EPC businesses can destroy cash; order-book execution risk is high
D/E at 0.48 and borrowings at INR 982 Cr and rising — moderate leverage but will expand further as order book grows
Order-book concentration in marine, MRT, and government infra makes revenue lumpy and subject to policy/election-cycle delays
red_flags: Market cap INR 11,136 Cr — far outside my 100–1,000 Cr sweet spot; institutional discovery is complete
P/E of 23.7x for an EPC contractor is demanding; construction margins at 7.74% leave little room for project cost overruns
FCF/PAT conversion is extremely poor (INR 30 Cr FCF vs INR 373 Cr PAT in FY25) — profits are largely paper until collected from government clients
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Cemindia has genuinely impressive operational metrics for a construction company — a 27.6% ROCE is almost unheard of in EPC and reflects their specialization in technically complex marine structures, MRT systems, and underground tunnelling where competition is thin and margins are relatively protected. The revenue trajectory (INR 2,728 Cr in FY21 to INR 9,097 Cr in FY25) is the kind of transformation story I love, and promoter at 67% signals conviction. If I had found this at INR 1,000–2,000 Cr market cap three years ago, it would have been a strong SMILE candidate.

Today the price already reflects most of this story. At P/E 23.7x for a business where FCF conversion is nearly zero (receivables from government clients drag), the margin of safety is thin. The name change from ITD Cementation to Cemindia in 2025 and the new Renew Exim parentage introduce integration risk. I would watch this for a 30–40% correction to bring it to P/E 14–16x before getting excited.
